role.altitude: The research assistant keeps setting codebooks, double-coding samples, pretesting questionnaires and coaching interviewers; coding paper forms, first-pass coding of open answers, logging reimbursements and compiling progress counts shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking proposed codes against a double-coded sample
role.ambitious_version: An assistant who codes every open answer in a survey instead of a sample, with agreement measured.

tasks.short: Set up the codebook, code data from paper forms and open answers in preparation for computer entry, and check coding consistency on a double-coded sample.

steps.what: Research assistant sets up the codebook with the researcher
Respondent answers the closed questions in the online survey, which stores them coded
Interviewer records closed answers on the tablet form, which stores them coded
Research assistant codes closed answers from paper forms for computer entry
Research assistant codes open answers by the codebook

loop.input: Pseudonymised open answers and the codebook with examples.
loop.output: A proposed code per answer with a short reason.
loop.check: The assistant reads each open answer with its proposed code and reason against the codebook definition, then confirms or changes the code; agreement with a double-coded sample is measured each wave.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword rules miss answers that say the same thing in other words.

steps.what: Research assistant double-codes a sample and checks coding consistency

tasks.design: Closed answers are captured already coded in the online survey or the interviewers' tablet forms, so only remaining paper forms are coded by hand. For open answers, a classifying step proposes a code from the codebook with a reason, on pseudonymised text in an EU-hosted or local tool, and the assistant confirms or changes each one. The assistant double-codes a sample to measure agreement.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every paper form and open answer was coded by hand into spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Online and tablet data capture, and coding tools that propose codes with reasons.
tasks.still_hard: Answers that fit no code or several.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing when the codebook itself needs a new code.

ambition.what: Code all open answers instead of a sample.

tasks.altitude: Less hand coding; codebook judgement stays.

evidence.claim: A qualitative analysis tool suggests codes with reasons, with EU storage or a local model.
A zero-shot model beat crowd workers on 4 of 5 text coding tasks at under USD 0.003 per item.
Research use of personal data needs safeguards such as pseudonymisation.

assumptions: Boundary: coding data for entry; analysis is separate.

Input contract for s2: answers captured coded by respondents online (s1b) and by interviewers on tablets (s1c), each shown at share 1, for about 70% of forms; s2 keeps 35: about 30 for paper forms still coded by hand and about 5 for checking captured data.
Codebook and double-coding keep their full time.
unknowns: Agreement between proposed and confirmed codes per study.
research_questions: Does coder agreement hold when proposals are used?

already_counted.description: Research assistant confirms or changes proposed codes.

incremental.description: Research assistant adds examples to the codebook for the coding step.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: paper-heavy studies with long open answers, so most closed answers are still coded by hand (s2 keeps 70) and proposals help less (s3 keeps 80) (15.2); high: online surveys with short open answers (34.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Track laboratory supplies and orders, collect participant details and log participant reimbursement, have the list approved, submit it to finance and track expenses against the budget.

steps.what: Study participant enters bank details in the study's reimbursement form
Research assistant tracks laboratory supplies and prepares orders when stock is low
Research assistant checks the final order: items and quantities against stock and the project budget, and the supplier it goes to
Research assistant places the checked order in the procurement system
Research assistant logs participant reimbursement: sessions, amounts and bank details
Project leader approves the final reimbursement list
Research assistant checks the approved list before submitting: that it is the version the project leader approved, amounts against sessions attended, bank details, and the finance mailbox it goes to
Research assistant submits the approved list to finance for payment
Research assistant tracks expenses against the project budget

approvals.approved_version: The reimbursement list with participants, sessions, amounts and bank details exactly as approved by the project leader in s4 and checked by the assistant in s4b, submitted once to finance for payment; any change goes back for approval and a new check.
The supply order with its items, quantities and supplier exactly as checked by the assistant in s2b, placed once in the procurement system on the project code; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Supplies have reorder points in the procurement system, which reminds the assistant when stock falls below them. Participants enter their bank details in a reimbursement form kept apart from the research data, and the session list from the booking tool fills sessions and amounts, so the reimbursement list builds itself; the assistant checks it. The project leader approves; the assistant checks that list and submits it once to finance. Supply orders are checked and placed by the assistant. Finance books all expenses on the project code, and a budget report replaces the assistant's spreadsheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplies, reimbursements and budgets were kept in separate spreadsheets typed from receipts and forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Reorder points, online forms and budget reports per project code.
tasks.still_hard: Participants without a bank account or with wrong details.
tasks.human_edge: Treating participants fairly when a session goes wrong.
tasks.altitude: Less bookkeeping; judgement on exceptions stays.

evidence.claim: Records apps with entry rules replace spreadsheets as glue.
Research use of personal data needs safeguards such as keeping identifying data apart.

assumptions: Boundary: tracking supplies, reimbursements and expenses; payment by finance is outside.

Input contract for s3: bank details entered by participants in the form (s1) and sessions from the booking tool kept by the assistant; about 80% of participants use the form; s3 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s6: invoices and payments booked by finance on the project code.
Participants' effort on the form is about what the paper form took and sits in s1 (share 1).
unknowns: Share of participants paid in cash or vouchers.

incremental.description: Research assistant helps participants who cannot use the form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small studies with cash payments, so the list is still built by hand (s3 keeps 90), and many costs outside the project code (s6 keeps 80) (16.3); high: large studies with many paid participants using the form (38.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search validated scales and earlier questionnaires, draft questions and answer categories, build the survey instruments with routing in the survey tool and pretest them.

steps.what: Research assistant searches validated scales and earlier questionnaires

loop.input: The research questions and open question banks and journal databases.
loop.output: A list of scales and items with their sources.
loop.check: The assistant opens every source and copies items only from the source itself.
loop.why_not_simpler: Scales are named differently across fields.

steps.what: Research assistant drafts questions and answer categories for the questionnaires
Research assistant builds the questionnaire with routing in the survey tool
Research assistant pretests the questionnaire with test respondents

tasks.design: A search step over question banks and journals lists validated scales with sources, and the assistant copies items only from the source. Drafting questions stays with the assistant and researcher. The survey tool's routing is tested with simulated test runs through every path before the pretest. Pretesting stays human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scales were found through colleagues and memory, and routing was tested by clicking through.
tasks.enabler_now: Searchable question banks and survey tools with test runs.
tasks.still_hard: Questions that respondents read differently than intended.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in a pretest that a question confuses people.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and clicking; question design stays.

reach.learn: Whether more validated scales are used.

evidence.claim: Generated citations were often invented: 55% and 18% for two models.
Survey tools can run simulated responses through every routing path.

assumptions: Boundary: designing and testing the instrument; fieldwork is outside.
Drafting and pretesting keep their full or nearly full time.
unknowns: How many new instruments are designed per year.
research_questions: Do routing errors found in fieldwork fall?

already_counted.description: Research assistant opens and checks every listed source.

incremental.description: Research assistant sets up simulated test runs per survey.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short questionnaires on familiar topics, so search and routing tests save little (s1 and s3 keep 90) (4.5); high: long instruments with complex routing (12.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Brief and train survey interviewers, assign respondents, monitor progress and response rates, check interview quality and handle interviewers' problems to supervise the work of survey interviewers.

steps.what: Research assistant briefs and trains survey interviewers
Research assistant assigns respondents and addresses to interviewers
Research assistant checks the final assignments: respondents and addresses per interviewer and area, and workloads
Research assistant releases the checked assignments to the interviewers' tablets
Interviewer records each visit outcome on the tablet: completed, refused or not reached
Research assistant monitors progress and response rates
Research assistant selects interviews for back-checks from the survey tool's random draw
Research assistant checks interview quality with back-checks and recordings
Research assistant handles interviewers' questions and problems

tasks.design: The survey tool's sample management proposes respondents by area per interviewer; the assistant adjusts, checks and releases the assignments once. Interviewers' tablets sync completed and refused interviews, so a fieldwork dashboard shows progress and response rates by area and wave instead of counts gathered from mailed reports. The tool also selects random interviews for back-checks. Training, judging quality and helping interviewers stay human. Because the dashboard can show figures per interviewer, the works council agrees its use first.

approvals.approved_version: The respondent and address assignments per interviewer exactly as checked by the assistant in s2b, released once to the interviewers' tablets for this wave; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was collected from interviewers' mails and typed into spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Survey tools with sample management and synced fieldwork data.
tasks.human_edge: Coaching an interviewer through a tough week.

reach.learn: Whether earlier support improves response rates.

evidence.claim: Systems fit to monitor staff performance need works council consent.
Survey tools sync tablet interviews and show fieldwork progress.

assumptions: Boundary: supervising interviewers during fieldwork; recruiting them is outside.

Input contract for s3: completed, refused and not-reached outcomes recorded by interviewers on their tablets (s2d, share 1, other role), about the time a mailed report took; about 85% of fieldwork is on tablets; s3 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: the sample file with addresses from the researcher.
Training and problem solving keep their full time.
Pricing of s4: the tool's random draw replaces drawing by hand, about 60% of selecting; targeted back-checks on interviewers with odd patterns are still picked by the assistant.
research_questions: Do response rates improve with earlier support?

incremental.description: Research assistant sets dashboard views agreed with the works council.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small teams of interviewers in one city, so automatic assignment saves little (s2 keeps 90) and many reports still come by mail (s3 keeps 80) (8.0); high: national fieldwork with many interviewers (19.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
